assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for last season's spring insert press file (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live merge template).

Document: single insert page, 5.5 x 8.5 in (half-letter) PORTRAIT, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 in bleed on all four edges), all fonts embedded and subset. This is the exact file the printer still holds and reruns.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (reads as several tidy fields):
- Top: the house MARK (kettle-in-ring lockup) placed small and centered above a thin rule.
- Header: 'Emberwell Brew House' in the display serif, 'Good coffee, kept close' beneath in the humanist sans.
- Left column: the PLATES list - each line is a dish NAME in the display serif, a one-line DESCRIPTION in the sans, then a PRICE set flush right at the end of the line with a faint leader rule running out to it.
- Right column: the DRINKS list, set the same way, name then price at the end of the line, over a faint Steam panel.
- One placed DISH PHOTOGRAPH: a single silhouetted plate given air, lower right.
- Bottom: the fixed ALLERGEN line, small, in the sans.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The dish NAME, its DESCRIPTION and its PRICE are ONE continuous text story flowing down the column - name, description and price number are a single run per line, NOT three addressable frames and NOT a separate price frame. Each price can only be reached by its character offset inside the shared story, and that offset depends on the exact string the story holds, not on where the price sits on the printed page.
- On conversion the whole insert exposes roughly: two long threaded text frames (plates story, drinks story), one small text frame (allergen), ONE graphic frame (the dish photo), and the placed mark artwork. Conversion granularity is a property of how the PDF was produced and is not controllable; the tidy printed columns are not evidence of separate frames.
- There is exactly ONE graphic frame (the dish photo) to bind a per-store picture into.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be produced from this file however the render or export is called. This has to be stated to the printer, not assumed away.

FIELD ROLES the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not as visible placeholder tokens): DISH_NAME | DISH_DESC | PRICE | DRINK_NAME | DRINK_PRICE | ALLERGEN | FEATURED_PHOTO (one graphic frame) | MARK (placed artwork).

Colours: Warm Cream #F4EDE0 ground, Roast #3B2A21 body and dish names, Ember #B4552D thin rules and the price accent, Kettle Brass #A8823F the mark's ring, Slate Ink #2B2622 the allergen line, Steam #D8CBB8 the faint panel behind the drinks column.
Type: a warm high-contrast display serif for names and header (generously leaded); a quiet humanist sans for descriptions, prices and the allergen line.

FOOTER AND FEATURE (per-store non-numeric content, joined per store from the store directory): last season's file also carries, below the allergen line, a small FIXED-HEIGHT FOOTER frame holding one sample store's street address and opening hours, and above the plates a single ON NOW line in a one-line frame for the room's rotating tap or special. Both were set to that one short sample store, so they are sized to short text; a per-store address, hours line or feature of any real length OVERSETS these frames and the tail clips at trim, and the merge reports success. Additional field roles the downstream mapping must also resolve (present as content, not visible tokens), joined per store from the store directory: STORE_ADDRESS | STORE_HOURS | FEATURE.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED:
- Top: the house MARK (kettle-in-ring lockup) small and centered above a thin rule.
- Header: 'Emberwell Brew House' in the display serif, 'Good coffee, kept close' beneath in the humanist sans.
- A single ON NOW line under the header, in the sans, for the room's rotating tap or special.
- DRINKS: the coffee program and cold drinks, each line a drink NAME at the left and its PRICE flush right, aligned to a tab, over a faint Steam panel. NO plates section anywhere.
- A short FROM THE CASE line naming the pastry/case items (no prices), in the sans.
- FOOTER: the room's STREET ADDRESS and its HOURS, small, in the sans.
- Bottom: the fixed ALLERGEN line, small, in the sans.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap, and it is NOT the plates file's trap):
- The drink NAME and its PRICE are set as ONE tab-aligned TWO-COLUMN story: name, tab, price on each line, flowing down the column as a single story. Each price is reached by its character offset inside THIS story, which sits at completely different positions than the plates file's single flow; a mapping or offset set built against the plates template binds to nothing here.
- On conversion this card exposes roughly: one two-column drinks story, one short ON NOW frame, one short FROM THE CASE story, one small FOOTER frame (address + hours), one allergen frame, and the placed mark artwork.
- There is NO graphic frame anywhere on this card, because the counter tier carries no dish photograph. The per-store picture column has nothing to bind into here and must NOT be passed to this template's merge.
- The FOOTER frame and the ON NOW frame were set to ONE short sample store, so they are sized to short text; a per-store address, hours line or feature of real length OVERSETS them and the tail clips at trim on merge, with the merge reporting success.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be produced from this file however the render or export is called. This has to be stated to the printer, not assumed away.

FIELD ROLES the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens), joined per store from the price sheet and the store directory: DRINK_NAME | DRINK_PRICE | FEATURE (on now) | STORE_ADDRESS | STORE_HOURS | ALLERGEN | MARK (placed artwork). NOTE: there is NO DISH_NAME, NO DISH_DESC, NO plates PRICE column and NO FEATURED_PHOTO on this template.

Colours: Warm Cream #F4EDE0 ground, Roast #3B2A21 body and drink names, Ember #B4552D thin rules and the price accent, Kettle Brass #A8823F the mark's ring, Slate Ink #2B2622 the allergen and footer lines, Steam #D8CBB8 the faint panel behind the drinks.

assets.prompt: Extreme close-up smartphone macro photograph of a small round enamel lapel pin fastened to the strap of a dark canvas apron. The pin carries a compound brand lockup: a solid KETTLE silhouette (a squat stovetop kettle with a curved spout and a handle) enameled in warm rust-orange at the centre, enclosed by a RING of letterspaced small-cap letters reading E M B E R W E L L B R E W H O U S E enameled in deep dark brown, struck on polished plated brass metal. The pin face is domed and reflective. CRITICALLY, uneven light throws a bright specular band across the LOWER-LEFT of the ring, and there the dark-brown enamel of the letters and the brass plating fall to almost the same tonal value so the letters nearly disappear into the metal along that shadowed-then-glared third. The enclosed centre inside the ring is fully filled by the kettle, a true compound lockup with an enclosed interior. Realistic enamel texture, tiny reflections, casual real-world close-up, not a studio shot. No other text and no real brand names.

assets.content:
EMBERWELL BREW HOUSE - SPRING INSERT COPY (approved wording; the allergen line is fixed and cannot change)

PLATES
Ember Skillet Hash - Root vegetables and a farm egg, crisped in the cast iron, kept simple.
Kettle Roast Chicken - Half a bird, brined overnight and roasted, with the day's greens.
Braised Short Rib - A long braise, root mash, a spoon of pan gravy.
Smoked Trout Plate - Trout smoked in the house, rye toast, pickled onion.

THIS SEASON (three seasonal lines this spring)
Winter Squash Toast - Roasted squash on grilled levain, brown butter, sage.
Maple Pork Belly - Maple-glazed belly, cider apples, a little mustard.
Spiced Pear Tart - Poached pear, warm spice, a short crust.

DRINKS
House Drip - The daily roast, black or with cream.
Cortado - Two shots and a little steamed milk, no more.
Cold Brew - Slow steeped overnight, poured over ice.
Maple Oat Latte - Espresso, oat milk, a line of maple.
Emberwell Stout - On until the barrel is done, then it is not.
Spiced Chai - Our house blend, steamed, a little heat.

ALLERGEN STATEMENT (fixed - do not reword)
Please tell us about any allergies before you order. Our kitchens handle gluten, dairy, eggs, nuts and shellfish in a small space, and we cannot promise any dish is free of them.

A NOTE ON PRICE
Prices sit quiet at the end of the line. No specials language, no combos, no value words. Every room sets its own price from the operations sheet.
